taxonomyNote: NatureServe (McKelvy and Burbrink 2017) treats L. rhombomaculata (mole kingsnake) and L. occipitolineata as distinct species; Animal Diversity Web still lists them as subspecies of L. calligaster.
fieldMarks: Tan, grey-brown or yellow-brown with reddish-brown dorsal blotches alternating with smaller lateral blotches; pale or yellowish belly.
Older snakes lose the pattern with age; 19-27 rows of smooth scales.
Often mistaken for a copperhead: copperheads have brown hourglass crossbands, kingsnakes have blotches.
behavior: Nocturnal and mostly solitary; active about April to mid-October and hibernates November-March in burrows or rock ledges.
Spends about 75% of radio-tracked time underground; can climb and swim.
Eats mice and voles, amphibians, snakes, lizards and birds and their eggs.
habitat: Open habitats: fields, farmland, woodlots, rocky hillsides, favouring prairie and pasture on light soils.
range: Populations west of the Mississippi River across the plains states and east across the Mississippi embayment to Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, western Tennessee and northern Mississippi (NatureServe); the wider group reaches Maryland and Florida.

lookalikes.name: Copperhead
lookalikes.howToTell: Copperheads have brown hourglass crossbands; prairie and mole kingsnakes have dorsal blotches.
